prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-04-16, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-04-16):
| Current ratio           | 0.90 |
| Retained earnings       | 73,165M |
| Current liabilities     | 34,477M |
| Current assets          | 30,916M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,383M |
| Total liabilities       | 89,110M |
| Total assets            | 110,646M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,213M |
| Revenue                 | 19,443M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows a high leverage profile with total liabilities at 89,110M against assets of 110,646M, implying substantial indebtedness. Liquidity is constrained with a current ratio of 0.90, suggesting short-term refinancing risk despite solid earnings (EBIT 3,213M) and sizable retained earnings. Absence of interest coverage data limits precision, but the combination of leverage and liquidity weakness points to a mid-investment-grade rating rather than a strong investment-grade or high-yield rating.

DECISION: BBB-
